name: Maine
lawPassed: Maine's packaging EPR law (LD 1541, 38 M.R.S. §2146, enacted July 2021) was amended by LD 1423 (signed June 20, 2025). The program covers all consumer packaging material types regardless of substrate — plastic (including film/poly bags and flexible packaging), paper (including paper bags and paper-based packaging), glass, metal, and cardboard. Implementation is stalled: the Stewardship Organization RFP closed August 18, 2026 with zero proposals submitted, and on September 11, 2026 Maine DEP announced it will revise and reissue the RFP.
status: Maine DEP published its Stewardship Organization RFP on June 15, 2026, but received no proposals by the August 18, 2026 deadline; Circular Action Alliance — the sole expected bidder and the PRO in all six other EPR states — declined to bid, citing misalignment between the RFP scope and its operational model. On September 11, 2026, DEP announced it will revise the RFP and reissue it. With no Stewardship Organization under contract, producers currently have no active registration, reporting, or fee obligations, and all previously stated implementation dates (including late-2026 registration and invoicing) are no longer in effect.

name: Washington
lawPassed: Washington E2SSB 5284 (Recycling Reform Act) signed into law May 17, 2025; effective July 27, 2025. The law establishes an EPR program covering glass, plastic (including wraps, films, and bags), paper, and metal packaging and paper products sold to residential consumers. The Washington Department of Ecology is now in active Phase 1 implementation: rulemaking underway (Chapter 173-950 WAC), a preliminary statewide collection list was open for public comment August 5–19, 2026, and finalized collection lists are due by October 2026.
status: The law (codified as Chapter 70A.208 RCW) requires producers of covered packaging and paper products to join or form a Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) by July 1, 2026, with the PRO required to have registered with Ecology by March 1, 2026. Circular Action Alliance (CAA) registered as the PRO on behalf of producers. Ecology is conducting rulemaking and published preliminary statewide collection lists for public comment in August 2026; final lists are due by October 1, 2026. Full program implementation, including curbside recycling cost reimbursements to service providers, begins January 1, 2030.

name: Maryland
lawPassed: Maryland SB 901 (Packaging and Paper Products – Producer Responsibility Plans Act) was signed into law on May 13, 2025, and its first implementing regulations (COMAR 26.04.14) became effective May 25, 2026. The law covers all packaging and paper products — including primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging materials such as plastic film/bags, paper bags, and mesh/bulk-good bags — sold, offered for sale, imported, or distributed in Maryland.
status: The program is now in its active registration and early-compliance phase: implementing regulations took effect May 25, 2026, and CAA (the only currently registered PRO) was required to submit its producer, brand, and material list to MDE by July 1, 2026. Fees are not yet active; the PRO five-year producer responsibility plan is due July 1, 2028, after which a cost-share ramp begins (50% of net recycling costs by 2028, 75% by 2029, 90% by 2030). MDE has indicated additional rulemakings will follow to address full reporting categories, fee structures, and other program details.

name: California
lawPassed: California SB 54 (Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act), enacted June 2022; permanent implementing regulations approved by the Office of Administrative Law on May 1, 2026 and now in effect. The program covers all single-use packaging (including plastic film, bags, flexible packaging, paper-based packaging, and food service ware) sold, distributed, or imported into California.
status: Permanent regulations took effect May 1, 2026, triggering immediate producer registration and reporting obligations. CAA submitted its draft California Program Plan to the SB 54 Advisory Board on June 15, 2026; a public comment period closed August 14, 2026, and CAA must submit the final Program Plan to CalRecycle by October 13, 2026 for approval by January 1, 2027, when full program enforcement begins. Two active lawsuits challenge the regulations — a June 2, 2026 state court suit by NRDC/Californians Against Waste over alleged regulatory loopholes, and a June 22, 2026 federal suit by a 17-state coalition and NAW raising constitutional objections — but neither has resulted in a stay or injunction, and compliance obligations remain in effect.

name: Colorado
lawPassed: Colorado HB22-1355 (Producer Responsibility Program for Statewide Recycling Act), signed June 3, 2022, covering all packaging materials and paper products (including poly bags, plastic film, paper, and other flexible/rigid packaging). The program entered active implementation as of January 1, 2026, with producer dues obligations live. Within the last 30 days, the ILMA lawsuit against CDPHE (filed March 12, 2026) remains pending in Denver District Court with no injunction in place, and SB26-192 (EPR dues appeal bill) was introduced in the 2026 session but did not advance to enactment before the legislature adjourned May 13, 2026.
status: Colorado's EPR program is fully live: producers of all covered packaging and paper products have been required to register with CAA since October 2024, submit supply reports (2024 data due July 31, 2025; 2025 data due May 31, 2026), and pay annual dues beginning January 2026. CDPHE approved CAA's final program plan on December 9, 2025, with CAA required to begin full implementation by June 9, 2026. A legal challenge by the Independent Lubricant Manufacturers Association (ILMA) filed March 12, 2026 in Denver District Court alleges constitutional and statutory violations in CDPHE's program implementation; no injunction has been issued and the program continues to operate.

name: Illinois
lawPassed: Illinois has no enacted packaging EPR law. Public Act 103-0383 (SB 1555, signed July 2023) established the Statewide Recycling Needs Assessment Advisory Council and directed Illinois EPA to conduct a packaging and paper products needs assessment, with final recommendations due to the General Assembly and Governor by December 1, 2026. Separately, HB 4064 (the Extended Producer Responsibility and Recycling Refund Act), introduced May 21, 2025, is pending in the House Rules Committee with no action since introduction. Senate companion SB 1817 contains only a short-title provision and no substantive text.
status: HB 4064 is stalled in the House Rules Committee, with legislative movement effectively gated on the Statewide Recycling Needs Assessment report due December 1, 2026. No producer obligations, fees, or PRO requirements are in effect in Illinois today. The needs assessment advisory council is actively meeting and is expected to deliver policy recommendations that could shape a full EPR bill in the 2027 session.

name: New Jersey
lawPassed: New Jersey S673 / A3744 (Packaging and Paper Product Stewardship Act) — carry-over of prior S3398 — reintroduced January 13, 2026 in the 2026-2027 legislative session; pending in the Senate Environment and Energy Committee with no floor vote taken.
status: S673 and companion A3744 were re-filed on January 13, 2026 as carry-overs of S3398 (which cleared the Senate Environment and Energy Committee in February 2025 but stalled before a full floor vote). The bill would require producers of all packaging and paper products to join a PRO or submit their own stewardship plan, mandating a 50% reduction in single-use packaging over ten years, 65% recycling rates, and full recyclability or compostability of all packaging by 2034. As of the most recent reporting (June–July 2026), the bill remains pending in committee with no enacted law; New Jersey is one of only two states whose EPR packaging bills carry over into 2027.

name: New York
lawPassed: New York Packaging Reduction and Recycling Infrastructure Act (PRRIA), SB 1464A / A1749A — failed to pass for the third consecutive session in June 2026; bill remains alive but unenacted, with a new session expected in 2027.
status: The 2026 New York legislature adjourned in June 2026 without voting on SB 1464A / A1749A. The amended bill — which covers all packaging types including plastic film, bags, paper, and other materials, and would require producers with over $5M in annual revenue and more than 2 tons of annual packaging waste to reduce packaging 10% within 3 years and 30% within 12 years — passed the Senate three consecutive years (2024, 2025, and a version in 2026) but stalled in the Assembly each time. In late April 2026, sponsors introduced nearly 150 amendments aligning definitions and timelines with Minnesota and California, removing five toxic substances, and consolidating enforcement under DEC and the Attorney General; those changes were not sufficient to secure Assembly passage before adjournment.

name: Hawaii
lawPassed: HB 750 (Act 103, Session Laws of Hawaii 2025) signed into law May 27, 2025. Requires the Hawaii Department of Health to conduct a statewide packaging EPR needs assessment covering packaging materials (paper, paperboard, cardboard, plastics, glass, metal, and mixed materials) and paper products. A companion full EPR bill, HB 1264, was introduced in the 2025 session but did not advance beyond committee referral. The 2026 legislative session adjourned sine die without new packaging EPR legislation passing; four non-binding labeling study resolutions introduced in March 2026 also did not advance. The needs assessment advisory board held its first meeting in late summer 2026 and is actively assembling.
status: HB 750 (Act 103) is enacted law; the Hawaii Department of Health began needs assessment work in July 2025 and the advisory council had its first formal meeting in late August/early September 2026. The final needs assessment report is due to the legislature by December 31, 2027. No comprehensive EPR program legislation has been enacted; Hawaii remains in a pre-EPR study phase.

name: Alaska
lawPassed: Alaska HB 25 (Disposable Food Service Ware) passed both chambers of the 34th Legislature with bipartisan support but was vetoed by Governor Mike Dunleavy on June 24–25, 2026. No veto override was pursued. No EPR packaging law of any kind is in effect in Alaska. The 34th Legislature has adjourned; any future bill must be reintroduced in the 35th Legislature (2027).
status: HB 25 would have banned single-use polystyrene foam foodware in restaurants and state agency operations starting January 1, 2027. Governor Dunleavy cited the bill's 2027 effective date as creating an unrealistic implementation timeline. No broader EPR packaging bill covering films, bags, or other packaging materials was introduced or advanced in Alaska during the 2025–2026 legislative session.

name: Florida
lawPassed: Florida has no EPR packaging law passed or pending. The 2026 legislative session (January 13 – March 13, 2026) adjourned without introducing or advancing any EPR packaging bill. HB 6225 (stand-alone EPR bill from a prior session) stalled in committee and has not been reintroduced. The state actively opposes EPR-related industry coordination: Florida AG Uthmeier led a multistate coalition sending antitrust warning letters in October 2025 to the Sustainable Packaging Coalition and Consumer Goods Forum, and follow-up letters to nearly 80 corporations in February 2026.
status: Florida's 2026 regular legislative session ended March 13, 2026 with no EPR packaging bill introduced or advanced.
